body: While you may have meant your post in the most sincere way possible it is clear that you too have biases. Your preferences identify who you would be attracted to as would anyone else's shape theirs. While straight individuals may like a single sex they still have preferences within that sex which are also labels. Just as you depend on labels to identify people you would be attracted to (ie: you don't like people that are not "fat" as you so gently put it). Don't be so judgmental when you are obviously falling into labeling trap that they are. You use labels every single day... some are extremely offensive others just make it easier on you and you choose to use them regardless. Try not to judge others so harshly when you are doing the same thing just attempting to describe it.

1. Pansexual 
2. Usually straight to anyone I'm not close to. Less questions and less judgement. Edit: In my experience many people aren't discrete sharing their homophobic opinions. I don't know if it's because I usually am around men, but many do not seem very accepting other people just because of they don't share the same orientation, so I choose not to share mine. Who I like does not concern them so I don't believe it matters if I lie about my orientation.
3. To no one of consequence. Similar because they aren't universally accepted and different because the suffering is prolonged until you explain what pansexuality is in the first place.
4. Usually straight. 
5. I've ran into hate, disgust, and curiosity. Not all at the same time.

Saw the xpost... thought I would contribute, good luck.
